newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Police teargas Khaleda's supporters, 100 injured.
newsitem.headline: Police teargas Khaleda's supporters, 100 injured.

text.p: Bangladesh police on Tuesday fired teargas and chased hundreds of rampaging supporters of former minister Begum Khaleda Zia in Dhaka.
Police said the activists of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) damaged several cars on Dhaka streets as they protested the filing of a corruption case against Khaleda by the government.
Witnesses said nearly 3,000 BNP supporters also protested government action on Monday to end a week-long revolt by prisoners in southwestern Jessore jail.
At least eight prisoners and one policeman were killed during a raid on the prison by security men.
The Bureau of Anti-corruption filed a corruption case against Khaleda on Sunday for her alleged misuse of power while in office, saying she gave police posts to several hundred of her party members.
The BNP lost an election in June to Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's Awami League.
BNP General Secretary Abdul Mannan Bhuyan said on Tuesday that the government had failed to end the prison revolt peacefully.
Bhuyan claimed that more than 100 BNP supporters were injured in Tuesday's police action and that the ruling party was out to eliminate its opponents by using force.
The witnesses, however, said about a dozen people including a newspaper photographer were injured in the police action.
Bhuyan said the filing of the case against Khaleda was an "example of the ruling party's politics of vengeance."
"We will be compelled to call a greater movement to oust the government unless it stops harrassment to our supporters and behaves democratically in running the country," he told the protest meeting.
Khaleda is due to return home on Wednesday from Saudi Arabia where she had received medical treatment for about three weeks.
